title: Keyboard-only navigation
learningObjectives: Explain keyboard-only navigation and apply it to accessible, reliable web development.

understand.concept: Keyboard access means users can reach and operate interactive elements without a pointer. Native buttons, links, and form controls support standard keyboard behaviour. Tab and Shift+Tab move focus; Enter and Space activate controls according to their semantics.
understand.whyItMatters: Keyboard-only testing reveals inaccessible custom controls, missing focus indicators, and unexpected focus order. It is a basic manual accessibility check.
understand.analogy: Keyboard navigation is a route through the interface that does not depend on a mouse or touchscreen.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; web protocols, browser behaviour, and accessibility requirements follow formal standards and platform implementations.

explain.narrative: The link provides a skip route; the native button is keyboard-operable. tabindex=-1 allows programmatic focus without adding the main region to the normal tab sequence.

practise.guidedTask: Complete a form using only Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, and arrow keys where appropriate. Record any inaccessible control.
practise.independentTask: Apply the concept to a small web page. Record the expected behaviour, how you tested it, and any limitations or fallbacks.
